claims.text: Formation and crystal-structure selection in rapidly thermally cycled noble-metal HEA nanoparticles are kinetically governed by suppressed precursor mobility.
The limited duration of rapid heating and cooling severely restricts atomic diffusion.
Restricted diffusion causes stochastic and spatially heterogeneous nucleation.
Stochastic heterogeneous nucleation traps metastable phases and produces phase separation, elemental segregation, and nonuniform morphology.
A modest extension of peak-temperature dwell time enhances local atomic rearrangement.
Enhanced atomic rearrangement from a longer dwell promotes formation of a uniform single-phase solid solution.
The initial material consists of more than five noble-metal precursors in nominally equal proportions.
Rapid thermal processing initially produces a kinetically trapped, disordered mixture.
Rapid thermal processing in the applicable regime uses heating rates on the order of 10^3–10^5 K/s followed by rapid cooling.
Rapid high-temperature processing and cooling can produce single-solid-solution HEA nanoparticles by suppressing secondary-phase formation.
Transient atomic ordering and early nucleation events mediate conversion of the heterogeneous state into a homogenized single phase.
Insufficient atomic mobility prevents full homogenization of the mixed precursors.
Local stochastic nuclei are rapidly quenched and thereby cause phase separation and elemental segregation.
A longer high-temperature dwell partially enables diffusion and produces more uniform elemental mixing.
Rapid heating and cooling without an added dwell yields multiple phases, elemental segregation, and poorly controlled particle morphology.
Extending the dwell time will increase elemental homogeneity and reduce phase-separated regions relative to the no-dwell baseline.
Extending the dwell time will lower the onset temperature for thermal decomposition.
The proposed mechanism applies to noble-metal HEA nanoparticles containing more than five elements under extreme nonequilibrium processing.
The mechanism may not apply when diffusion is already ample or when elemental diffusion rates are too disparate for a modest dwell extension to overcome.
